findings.suggested_fix: Give window close and OnBeforeQuit a dedicated shutdown request path. For an active cancellable job, remember the close request, cancel jobCancel, and finish closing after that job settles; for a non-cancellable save, remember the request and wait for it to settle. Preserve the existing dirty-review save/discard/cancel handling before closing, and keep Service.Close responsible for waiting for native work and closing storage. Add a focused test that requests quit during the first file of a batch, verifies later files never start, and verifies the pending quit resumes after cleanup.
findings.title: Quitting during import leaves the entire batch running
findings.why_it_matters: Closing the window or choosing Quit during a multi-file import does not cancel recognition or queue a quit: it only displays the busy message, and all remaining files continue importing. Both close handlers route through the navigation guard, which returns whenever a job is active, so the shutdown cancellation in Service.Close is unreachable until the user separately cancels or waits for the batch and requests quit again. A dedicated close flow can cancel the active import, await its existing cleanup, and then finish quitting without requiring hard interruption of an Apple API.

findings.title: Timeline loads every full report into memory
findings.why_it_matters: Opening a member timeline or refreshing after an import, save, or search reads every matching report, including up to 1 MiB of corrected text and up to 2 MiB of extraction JSON per report. The store decodes and validates every extraction, retains all reports in a slice, and the UI builds a control for every item. A household library with hundreds of reports can therefore cause large allocation spikes and slow timeline loads even though the list displays only title, date, and status.
